template_selections.selection_rationale: T01 is the only reference whose observed patterns cover every architecture section: numbered modules for the six steps, logo-tile grids for tool options, chip-row panels for the three signal groups, a staircase and tier stack for Step 4, categorized columns for the Step 6 lanes, and a terminal card for Closed-Won. It also has the highest native resolution for a 102-node design. T07 has the same structure but weaker numbering and lower resolution; T06 has no hub position and grows very tall.

runner_up.reason: Same structure, softer numbering, lower resolution.

limitations: No pattern for a hub with converging inputs; would need adaptation.
No connector labels.
Final modules are numbered; unnumbered downstream items need adaptation.
Includes a closed-lost branch pattern that must not be reused here.

design_direction.direction: Modular numbered-card infographic in the selected reference's design language, portrait orientation. No orientation or canvas constraint exists upstream, so portrait follows the reference.
Light, warm, near-white background; a subtle texture is optional. Keep it quiet so logos and chips stay legible.

Mostly neutral cards with one or two accents: one for number badges and the terminal card, one for the title. Signal groups and lanes may use soft distinct tints. Brand logos stay in original colors. Exact values are chosen in Step 08, not inferred from the reference.
Title > numbered step modules > sub-panels/lanes > chips/tiles. Steps 3 and 6 get the most area; downstream cards are smaller than modules; Closed-Won is the most emphasized element after the title.
Rounded cards with a thin outline and offset shadow, tabbed headers with number badges; sub-panels use a lighter container.

Rounded-square logo tiles with the name beneath; text-only tile when no approved logo exists. Signal categories and tool-less activities get no logos and no placeholders. No company or creator logo anywhere.
Thin dashed gray connectors with arrowheads in the gutters, for sequence only, plus one convergence group into the CRM. No connectors between stages and tiers, and none from activities to Closed-Won.
Generous gutters between modules for connector routing; consistent spacing within chip rows and tile grids; no overlapping text or icons.
No brand guidelines are supplied for this run (their absence is disclosed). Do not adopt the reference's title, wording, creator footer or company branding.

adaptation_requirements.description: Use six numbered modules only; render Slack Notification → Enroll in Sequences → CRM Tasks → Closed-Won as an unnumbered chain ending in the terminal card.
Do not reuse the reference start node, closed-lost card, or any outcome other than Closed-Won.

Make Step 3 the largest module: three labelled chip-row panels (first-, second-, third-party; 8/6/11 chips). Replace checkmark glyphs with neutral markers so categories do not read as completed tasks; no vendor logos.
Reduce the four categorized columns to two lanes (One-to-One, One-to-Many) for Step 6; attach tool icons to their own activity row; activities without tools show no tool and no placeholder.
Add a CRM hub treatment to Step 5: converge connectors from Steps 1–4 into the CRM Records element with one annotation, plus an onward connector to Step 6.

Combine staircase and tier stack in one Step 4 module side by side with the relationship note; no lines or alignment between individual stages and tiers; drop reference logos except the single HubSpot tile.
Replace the reference title, breadcrumb, header icon box and creator footer with this run's title, subtitle and optionality note; no footer identity or logo.
Keep the serpentine grid only if numbered order stays unambiguous; every step transition gets a directional dashed connector.
Pair HubSpot and Salesforce in a paired mini-card with the either/or marker in Step 5.
Logo tiles show the name beneath every logo; when Step 07 finds no approved logo, the tile shows the text label only. Repeated tools get a tile in every step.
